assessmentSummary.identity: A static split-squat position at a declared stance, depth, torso, support, and load contract, with a controlled hold, breathing, and exit.
currentCardFindings: Split Squat Iso Hold and Split Squat Isometric Hold are the same identity.
Supported bodyweight, unsupported bodyweight, and goblet-loaded mid-range holds are exact variants.
Four links have healthy oEmbed metadata only and remain unviewed candidate media.

currentCardSnapshot.description: Set the declared split stance and optional support, lower to the recorded mid-range knee and hip position, keep the front foot grounded and knee tracking, back heel raised, pelvis and ribs controlled, then hold with normal breathing for the prescribed quality time. End the effort and exit under control before depth changes, the knee drifts, the back knee rests, posture twists, breathing fails, or symptoms appear.

population.medicalScope: The card does not prescribe rehabilitation or clear symptoms; follow the athlete care plan and local scope.

claims: Privacy-enhanced YouTube embed URLs can be constructed with youtube-nocookie.com.

The candidate watch URLs returned oEmbed metadata on 2026-07-26; embed playback, full-video exact matching, cue and safety quality, captions, accessibility, reviewer identity, and approval remain unresolved.

evidence.sourceTitle: Joint angles of the ankle, knee, and hip and loading conditions during split squats
claims: The defining action is a static split-squat position at a declared depth.
Iso is an abbreviation of isometric and does not create a second identity.

evidence.sourceTitle: Joint angles of the ankle, knee, and hip and loading conditions during split squats
claims: Declare side, stance, depth, torso, support, load, hold duration, breathing, quality gate, and exit.
Dynamic repetitions, rear-foot elevation, perturbation, and jumps require separate definitions.

evidence.sourceTitle: Joint angles of the ankle, knee, and hip and loading conditions during split squats
claims: The split stance loads quadriceps and hip extensors with foot, ankle, hip, pelvis, and trunk stabilization.
Contribution varies with stance, depth, torso, load, and individual anatomy.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effects of step lengths on biomechanical characteristics of lower extremity during split squat movement
claims: Stride length and joint angles change lower-extremity mechanics, so exact setup must be recorded.
An isometric produces force without intentional joint motion at the declared position.

evidence.sourceTitle: Isometric training and long-term adaptations: Effects of muscle length, intensity, and intent: A systematic review
evidence.sourcePublisher: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
claims: Hand support lowers balance complexity; external load primarily raises physical demand and failure consequence.
Overall difficulty is the maximum of exercise complexity and physical demand.

evidence.sourceTitle: Isometric training and long-term adaptations: Effects of muscle length, intensity, and intent: A systematic review
evidence.sourcePublisher: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
claims: Isometric adaptations depend on task variables including muscle length, intensity, and intent.
Track stance, depth, load, hold time, local fatigue, postural drift, breathing, and side difference.

evidence.sourceTitle: Joint angles of the ankle, knee, and hip and loading conditions during split squats
claims: Use a stable surface and support, clear exit and set-down space, inspected load, and an exact depth marker.
Do not continue through symptoms, breath holding, collapse, or unsafe exit.

evidence.sourceTitle: Isometric training and long-term adaptations: Effects of muscle length, intensity, and intent: A systematic review
evidence.sourcePublisher: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
claims: Use submaximal quality holds with side-balanced sets and adequate rest; exact dose follows the intended adaptation.
Actual quality time ends at the first failed criterion.

evidence.sourceTitle: Joint angles of the ankle, knee, and hip and loading conditions during split squats
claims: Set stance and support, descend to recorded depth, establish foot-knee-pelvis-trunk position, breathe, hold, and exit before change.
Instruction names load, time, quality gate, stop rules, and set-down.

evidence.sourceTitle: Joint angles of the ankle, knee, and hip and loading conditions during split squats
claims: Stop for symptoms, giving way, breath holding, depth drift, knee collapse, load instability, or unsafe exit.
Use support, shallower depth, shorter time, or less load after review.

evidence.sourceTitle: Isometric training and long-term adaptations: Effects of muscle length, intensity, and intent: A systematic review
evidence.sourcePublisher: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
claims: Use supported bodyweight for access, unsupported bodyweight for capacity, and loaded holds only after position and exit are repeatable.
Count local lower-body and postural fatigue before speed, jump, or high-priority strength work.

evidence.sourceTitle: Joint angles of the ankle, knee, and hip and loading conditions during split squats
claims: Athlete guidance names expected effort, unexpected symptoms, self-checks, accessibility choices, and nonvideo instruction.
The athlete exits before failure and reports actual quality time.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effects of step lengths on biomechanical characteristics of lower extremity during split squat movement
claims: The coach verifies stance, depth, support, load, knee and foot, pelvis and trunk, breathing, and exit.
Record actual quality time and why the hold ended.

evidence.sourceTitle: Joint angles of the ankle, knee, and hip and loading conditions during split squats
claims: Stable support, shallower depth, shorter holds, bodyweight, and a wall-sit substitution can reduce balance or load demand.
A back-knee pad is an exit marker, not a resting surface in these variants.

evidence.sourceTitle: Joint angles of the ankle, knee, and hip and loading conditions during split squats
claims: Supported, unsupported, and goblet-loaded mid-range holds are exact variants; stance and duration are modifiers.
Rear-foot elevation, dynamic motion, perturbation, partner resistance, and jumps require separate definitions.
